verdict: Accepted. No remaining source review objection to the stateless navigation callback identity repair.
scope: Independent read-only source review plus one focused five-case run on the frozen AppNavigator and harness. No app edits, broad-suite execution, native/CI rerun, SDK lock or auth behavior changes.

artifactContext.ownerAnalysis: Hosted owns actual auth warning/read-storm counts and timeline; this review independently establishes the source feedback chain and repair behavior.

findings.result: AppNavigator subscribes to profile. The actual Profile load completion calls setAuthProfile with a newly merged object. An inline onUnhandledAction therefore changed on each successful profile publication. Installed useNavigationHelpers includes UnhandledActionContext in its memo dependencies; useNavigationCache depends on those helpers; useFocusEffect depends on navigation and reruns the effect while focused when that identity changes.

Both normal and password-recovery NavigationContainer branches now receive the same stateless module-level handleUnhandledNavigationAction. It closes over no account, profile, theme, navigation, request or component lifecycle value, so it cannot retain stale account state.

The function body is identical to the former inline handler: GO_BACK is ignored; other actions log only their optional type with the same prefix. It does not add a dev/prod condition or expose action payloads.

The focused harness executes installed Navigation helper/cache/focus code. It verifies that same-profile publication retains one focus read, genuine blur cleans up and genuine refocus reloads, while duplicate focus events remain suppressed.

No existing session revision subscription, account/setup/recovery gate, root navigator key, provider or route changed. The actual rendered root key differs for A→B→A revisions, even though the stateless diagnostic handler remains stable.

limits: Production AppNavigator, the actual extracted Profile load callback and installed Navigation 6 hook/cache implementations execute, but React scheduling, native hosts, navigation contexts/listeners and auth state are controlled doubles. This is not a complete mounted native application.
The profile test deterministically processes six subsequent render turns to expose the handler-driven feedback path; it is not a performance or network throughput benchmark.
The A→B→A test verifies actual root-key changes, not native view destruction, provider reinitialization or saved-account persistence. Those remain native acceptance checks.

No claim that this single repair eliminates every possible read storm or observed lock delay. The next native trace must confirm actual request/lock behavior without suppressing warnings or changing deadlines.
